title: Calculating the Take-Back on a Personal Checking Temporary Credit
content:
The amount taken back is the temporary credit standing on the Personal Checking account, netted against the corrective entries the bank has already made, less the part left with the owner, and never below zero.

**The temporary credit standing on the account** is every temporary credit entry posted to the account less every take-back entry already booked.

**The netting.** None of the corrective entries standing on the account is netted off the take-back. The netting is worked out on the corrective entries standing and rounded half-up to the cent before it is taken off.

**The part left with the owner.** No part of the temporary credit is left with the owner. The part left with the owner is worked out on the temporary credit standing and rounded half-up to the cent, and it is taken off after the netting.

The two subtractions are worked out on different figures: the netting on the corrective entries standing, the owner's part on the temporary credit standing. Each is rounded half-up to the cent on its own base, and the netting is taken off first.

The take-back is taken in whole steps of 5.00, rounded half-up.

**Worked example on hypothetical inputs.** An account carries temporary credit entries of 240.00 and 60.00, one take-back entry of 50.00 already booked, and corrective entries standing of 80.00.

| Quantity | Hypothetical figure |
|---|---|
| Temporary credit entries posted | 300.00 |
| Take-back entries already booked | 50.00 |
| Temporary credit standing on the account | 250.00 |
| Corrective entries standing | 80.00 |
| Netting, worked out on the corrective entries standing | 0.00 |
| Figure after the netting | 250.00 |
| Part left with the owner, worked out on the temporary credit standing | 0.00 |
| Figure after the owner's part is taken off | 250.00 |
| Take-back, in whole steps of 5.00, rounded half-up | 250.00 |

Where the figure after both subtractions would fall below zero, the take-back is 0.00, the rule holding it at zero before the rounding is taken.
